Big advertising agencies have been around forever and know what they're doing. If their ads weren't generating money they would change their business model. If you see the same ad for a while then someone's responding to it.

Advertisers have bots that make it look as if many people have viewed the ad. They then tell the companies "look at all the people who have seen the ad, what a success" when in reality, it may have been viewed by no one.

Ads have been around for a while now, the main thing you're missing is that they are cheap as fuck.

Advertisers are paying a fraction of a cent per view or whatever. So if they get 0.05% of ad viewers to buy the product they're making a ton of money for their client.

And think about what ads you see. It's either

1)Toys, targeted at kids who will bug their parents (who will presumable buy at least some toys)

2)Movies/games, targeted at people who will probably (according to the data collected) want to watch the movie/play the game

3)Stuff almost everyone needs to buy anyways (clothes, hygiene, a car). In those cases the point is that when the person needs new clothes/toothpaste/a new car they will know about the one that was being advertised and so will probably at least consider it while otherwise there would be no chance of them buying something they don't know about.

TL;DR: Advertising works very well. If it's failing on you either you're not the target or you don't realize it's working.

Over the course of my life, I've had 2 internet ads work for me. One was for a tshirt company that I ended up buying from several times, the other was an ad for Dexter before the series premiere. But most ads have a success rate of 0.01%. Think about how many people see a billboard on the highway. Most people don't react to most ads. But ads are also not very expensive. A billboard along a major interstate in a city might cost $5000 a month. Over the course of a month about you could estimate that 10% of the city's population will see the ad. Plus you'll get visitors from out of town that might see it too. So for $5000, about 100,000 people will see it. So the cost of one person seeing the ad is low and you don't need to gain many people before you have already recouped the cost of the ad. And then the new customers are likely to tell others about your business and now you are reaching more people.

Ads work because they are so low cost. Which is also why Pandora had trouble making a profit.
